TriData in tree/leaf-emission order: I implemented it (triangles appended at leaf-emission time, payload = the new slot index, so spatially neighbouring leaves index adjacent records) and A/B measured it against the same wide-node build with the original triangle order, in the same session, seed 1, scene-default.

Measured (render_ms_best):
- 3 reps x --benchmark 5: TREEORDER 45.95 / 48.90 / 46.31 (mean 47.1) vs ORIGINAL-ORDER 46.80 / 44.21 / 43.85 (mean 45.0).
- 3 reps x --benchmark 10 (tighter): TREEORDER 44.35 / 42.78 / 42.25 (mean 43.1, avg 48.9) vs ORIGINAL-ORDER 43.29 / 44.36 / 45.19 (mean 44.3, avg 48.2).

Decision: rejected and reverted. The two runs disagree in sign (best-ms favoured tree order by ~1.2 ms in the second pass, avg-ms favoured original order by ~0.7 ms), i.e. it sits well inside the session noise and shows no >=3% win, so I restored the original triangle order (copied scratch/wideA/src/bvh.cpp back over pathtracer/src/bvh.cpp) — simpler code and an unchanged TriData layout. The reason it likely doesn't help: the wide-node layout already stores each leaf's own AABB inline, so a leaf test is one cache line for the node plus one 48-byte TriData record, and the SAH tree is already spatially coherent, so re-indexing triangles buys little locality.

How I know: this is from my own round-3 log entries and tool results earlier in this session (the A/B loops above are the literal benchmark lines; scratch/wideA is the retained original-order control build), recovered from my compacted history segment art-000969. Current state of pathtracer/src/bvh.cpp confirms original triangle order (TriData filled up front, payload = original triangle index). No new work started.

Answer on the tree-order (leaf-emission-order) TriData experiment in round 3:

What it was: the BVH builder appended each triangle's TriData record at the moment its leaf was emitted, and stored that new index in the leaf payload, so records for spatially adjacent leaves sat adjacent in memory (better cache locality on the per-leaf triangle fetch) instead of the original OBJ triangle order.

What it measured: a wash — no win beyond session noise (the ±15% drift band I A/B against), well under my ≥3% keep threshold. It was in the same batch of "exact but cheap" ideas as the world-AABB shadow-ray guard, which also measured as a wash/very slight loss (guard runs 46.1/48.8/42.7 vs no-guard 44.0/43.9/45.0, means 45.9 vs 44.3). My own note at the time reads: "Traversal already segment-bounded for shadow rays; AABB guard and tree-order TriData were washes."

Decision: rejected. The change touched the builder, the payload semantics and the upload path for no measurable gain, so I reverted it and kept TriData in original triangle order — which is exactly what the adopted source documents today (pathtracer/src/bvh.cpp header: "the payload is the triangle index into TriData (which keeps the original triangle order)").

How I know: this is from my own earlier session notes, now in compacted memory segment art-000969 (the entries describing the leaf-emission edit to bvh.cpp and the follow-up note calling it a wash), corroborated by the live source in pathtracer/src/bvh.cpp, which still fills TriData up-front in original order rather than at leaf time. Round 3 settled on the unchanged default threadgroup size of 4x4 (16 threads per group, i.e. PT_TG=4); I did not adopt a different size.

How I know / how it was decided:
- First pass (PT_TG env override on the current wide1 build, 2 reps of --benchmark 5 --threads 8 --seed 1 on scene-default.json) suggested smaller groups might win: TG=2 gave bests 43.2/46.8 ms vs TG=4 at 50.4/47.0 ms, with TG=8 and TG=16 clearly worse. But that loop ran each config as its own contiguous block, so the ordering could have biased it (GPU clock warm-up/drift across the block).
- So I re-ran a clean interleaved A/B, alternating TG2 and TG4 runs in the same session (4 reps each). That decided it: mean best TG4 ~= 45.3 ms vs TG2 ~= 47.0 ms, i.e. TG2 was actually ~4% slower once the ordering bias was removed. TG4 also beat TG8/TG16.

Since no alternative cleared the >=3% win bar, the 4x4 group size stayed the default, and the round-3 gains came from the BVH changes (64-byte 2-wide inline-child nodes, single-triangle leaves, dropped unused barycentric data) rather than from retuning occupancy.

Round 3 kept the round-2 default threadgroup size of 4x4 = 16 threads per group (PT_TG=4 is the default; the sweep was driven by the PT_TG env override over 2, 4, 8, 16, i.e. 8, 16, 64, 256 threads per group).

How I know it: the first sweep on the wide-64B-node build looked like a win for smaller groups — TG=2 gave render_ms_best 43.2/46.8 vs TG=4's 50.4/47.0, with TG=8/16 worse still — but that comparison was confounded, because changing the group side length also changes which pixels land in the same threadgroup (coherence/order-in-block bias), not just occupancy. So I re-ran it as a clean interleaved same-session A/B with several alternating reps: TG4 mean best ≈ 45.3 ms vs TG2 ≈ 47.0 ms, i.e. TG=2 was actually ~3.7% slower once the ordering bias was removed. Since neither variant reached the >=3% win threshold in favor of a change (and TG2 was a loss), the 4x4 group stayed the default.

Round 3 kept the round-2 default threadgroup size: a 4x4 tile per threadgroup (PT_TG=4, i.e. 16 threads per group), dispatched as ceil(width/4) x ceil(height/4) groups.

How I know / how it was decided: I first swept PT_TG in {2, 4, 8, 16} on the round-3 'wide1' build (64-byte 2-wide BVH nodes, leaf=1 triangle) with back-to-back runs. That first pass looked like smaller groups won (TG=2 43.2/46.8 ms vs TG=4 50.4/47.0 ms, TG=8/16 worse), but the runs were grouped by configuration, so session drift could have biased it. I then re-ran the two finalists interleaved (TG2 and TG4 alternating in the same session, 4 reps each, --benchmark 5 --threads 8 --seed 1 on scene-default.json). The interleaved medians reversed the verdict: TG4 mean best ~45.3 ms vs TG2 ~47.0 ms, and a later clean A/B repeated 'TG4 kept (TG2 worse in clean A/B)'. Since no win reached the ~3% bar, I did not change the dispatch and left the default at 4x4.

For context on where that fits: the round-3 wins so far are the 64-byte wide nodes plus single-triangle leaves (~45.5 ms vs round-2 ~50.7 ms), a tree-quality sweep (bins 8/16/32/48, SAH cost 0.5/1/2) that was all noise so defaults stayed, and a 4-wide (128B node) experiment that rendered correctly (nodes 25760, depth 8) but measured ~47.2 vs ~44.7 ms in interleaved A/B, so it is a loss and is being rejected in favor of the 2-wide tree.

No — leaf2 (two triangles per BVH leaf) is NOT in pathtracer/ right now. The current build uses 64-byte wide nodes with single-triangle leaves (leaf = 1 triangle, triangle index in the payload word).

How I know:
1. Live evidence from this session: the current pathtracer/pathtracer binary prints "info: bvh nodes=69450 depth=16" — 69,450 = n-1 internal nodes, which is exactly the single-triangle-leaf tree. leaf2 measured 36,682 nodes / depth 15. pathtracer/src/bvh.cpp also carries the comment "Leaf size 1 measured fastest".
2. History (compacted segment art-001056): leaf2 was briefly adopted after a comparison that showed 33.5 ms vs 45.8 ms, but that baseline was the OLD 32-byte leaf-1 tree. After the 64-byte wide-node layout was introduced, a clean same-session 3-way A/B (3 reps, --benchmark 5, seed 1) gave:
   - pt_round_02 (32B, leaf1): 49.8 / 50.2 / 52.3 ms
   - scratch/wide1 (64B wide, leaf1): 44.3 / 45.7 / 46.4 ms  <- best
   - leaf2 (64B wide, 2 tris/leaf): 49.0 / 49.9 / 54.5 ms  <- loss
   So I wrote scratch/revert_leaf2.py and restored leaf=1 into pathtracer/ (verified afterwards: RMSE 0.476560 vs the frozen baseline 0.475898, i.e. 1.0014x).
3. Secondary reason to prefer leaf=1: leaf2 stores the union of two triangles' bounds, which changes closest-hit tie behaviour and produced a PFM that was not bit-identical to the leaf-1 build — a determinism/reference risk under the verifier's "same seed => bit-identical PFM" and RMSE-parity checks. leaf=1 keeps per-triangle bounds.

For context on where the round-3 work stands: adopted wins so far are the 64B wide-node layout plus dropping the never-shaded barycentrics from traversal (bit-identical output, md5 043b00ae...), ~45.5 ms vs round-2's ~50.7 ms. Rejected as measured losses: 4-wide 128B nodes (47.2 vs 45.9), 2-pixels-per-thread ILP (57-64 ms), analytic-floor-first tmax bounding (46.8 vs 44.4), the bunny-AABB shadow guard (wash), and BVH bin/SAH-cost sweeps (all noise).

How I know:
- Direct evidence from this session: running ./pathtracer/pathtracer prints "info: bvh nodes=69450 depth=16". That is the leaf=1 signature (69,451 triangles → 69,450 internal nodes). The leaf2 candidate measured "nodes 69450→36682, depth 15", and pathtracer/src/bvh.cpp still carries the leaf-size-1 builder with the comment "Leaf size 1 measured fastest".
- Why leaf2 was not kept: the earlier "big win" (leaf2 33.5 ms vs leaf1 45.8 ms) did not reproduce in the careful same-session A/Bs I run for every candidate. Later interleaved measurements of the adopted wide1/leaf1 build land at ~44–46 ms best, and no leaf2 build is present in pathtracer/. In addition, the leaf2 build's PFM md5 differed from the leaf1 build's at the same seed — expected because merging the two triangles' bounds into one leaf changes which triangle wins a near-tie closest-hit, and under this round's hard constraints (estimator/results must stay as close to the frozen baseline as possible) I treat that as a reason not to adopt a change unless it is a large, reproducible win, which it was not.

So the adopted round-3 state is: 64-byte wide nodes with both child AABBs inline + single-triangle leaves + dropped unused barycentric field, ~45 ms vs round-2's ~50 ms. The 4-wide (128-byte) node experiment I just measured is currently a wash/slight loss (46.1 vs 47.1 mean best across 4 interleaved reps), so it is on track to be rejected too.

Before shrinking BVH_STACK (it was 40 at the time), the first A/B was a single --benchmark 5 run of each binary in one session on scene-default (512x512, 64 spp, seed 1):

- 4-wide build (scratch/w4/pathtracer, 128B nodes, BVH_STACK=40): render_ms_best=49.501, gpu_ms_best=48.735, bvh nodes=25760, depth=8, samples=16777216.
